facts.statement: Hesperornithoides miessleri lived approximately between 157 and 145 million years ago, during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Hesperornithoides miessleri es la única especie conocida del género extinto Hesperornithoides de dinosaurio terópodo trodóntido que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 157 y 145 millones de años, entre el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: A well-preserved skeleton of Hesperornithoides was unexpectedly discovered in 2001 by a team from the Tate Geological Museum in Jimbo Quarry, Wyoming, near the excavation site of Supersaurus vivianae.
facts.quote: a well preserved skeleton wasn't found until in 2001, a field crew from the Tate Geological Museum supervised by William Wahl unexpectedly discovered the type skeleton Hesperornithoides in Jimbo Quarry, overlying the excavation site of Supersaurus vivianae, near Douglas, Wyoming.

facts.statement: The accidental discovery of the Hesperornithoides skeleton resulted in some fossils being damaged or lost.
facts.quote: The accidental discovery of the skeleton led to some of the fossils being damaged or lost.

facts.statement: The species Hesperornithoides miessleri was formally named and described in 2019 by Scott Hartman, Mickey Mortimer, William Wahl, Dean R. Lomax, Jessica Lippincott, and David M. Lovelace.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Hesperornithoides miessleri was named and described by Scott Hartman, Mickey Mortimer, William Wahl, Dean R. Lomax, Jessica Lippincott and David M. Lovelace in an article published on PeerJ.

facts.statement: The holotype individual of Hesperornithoides was estimated to be 89 cm long in 2019.
facts.quote: The length of the holotype individual was in 2019 estimated at 89 cm long.

facts.statement: The Hesperornithoides specimen is considered to represent either an adult or a subadult individual.
facts.quote: The specimen may represent an adult or subadult individual, due to the lack of cranial and body proportions associated with juvenile individuals.

facts.statement: The jugal bone of Hesperornithoides is pneumatic.
facts.quote: The jugal bone is pneumatised.

facts.statement: The third claw of the hand in Hesperornithoides is about the same size as the second claw.
facts.quote: The third claw of the hand is about as large as the second claw.

facts.statement: The Hesperornithoides specimen preserves keratin sheaths on the tips of several toe and hand claws.
facts.quote: Notably, the specimen preserves some keratin sheaths on the distal end of several pedal and manual unguals.

facts.statement: In 2019, Hesperornithoides was classified within the Troodontidae family in a relatively basal position alongside Daliansaurus, Xixiasaurus, and Sinusonasus.
facts.quote: In 2019, Hesperornithoides was placed in the Troodontidae, in a relatively basal position, in a clade with Daliansaurus, Xixiasaurus and Sinusonasus, as shown in the cladogram below:

facts.statement: Hesperornithoides belongs to the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: familia: Troodontidae

facts.statement: The generic name Hesperornithoides is derived from Greek words meaning "western bird form".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek Ἑσπερίς, Hesperis, "western", ὄρνις, ornis, "bird", and ~eides, "form".

facts.statement: The specific name miessleri honors the Miessler family for their support of the research project.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Miessler family for its support of the project.

facts.statement: In 2019, Hesperornithoides was placed in the family Troodontidae in a relatively basal position.
facts.quote: En 2019, Hesperornithoides fue situado en la familia Troodontidae en una posición relativamente basal

facts.statement: Unpublished phylogenetic analyses presented at the 2017 SVP conference determined that the specimen known as "Lori" was a relative of Sinovenator.
facts.quote: Análisis filogenéticos sin publicar presentados en la conferencia de la SVP en 2017 determinaron que "Lori" era un pariente de Sinovenator

facts.statement: The presence of this advanced maniraptoran alongside other genera like Anchiornis and Eosinopteryx in Jurassic sediments refutes the argument of the "temporal paradox" used by those opposing the consensus that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
facts.quote: La presencia de este avanzado maniraptorano junto con varios otros géneros, tales como Anchiornis y Eosinopteryx en sedimentos del Jurásico es una contundente refutación al argumento de la "paradoja temporal"

facts.statement: The parent group of Hesperornithoides is Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Hesperornithoides is classified under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Hesperornithoides is Hesperornithoides miessleri.
facts.quote: Type species: Hesperornithoides miessleri

facts.statement: Hesperornithoides lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Hesperornithoides in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: Hesperornithoides lived in a relatively open landscape with watercourses, few elevations, and few trees.
facts.quote: Vivió en un paisaje relativamente abierto y con cursos de agua, con escasas elevaciones y pocos árboles

facts.statement: Apart from Avialae, many paravian groups had some members with certain flight capabilities.
facts.quote: Aparte de los Avialae, muchos grupos de paravianos tenían algunos miembros con cierta capacidad de vuelo

facts.statement: These specimens showed adaptations for an arboreal lifestyle, indicating that flight developed multiple times when species evolved traits and behaviors useful for climbing trees or other vertical surfaces.
facts.quote: Estos ejemplares mostraban adaptaciones para un estilo de vida arborícola, lo que indica que el vuelo se desarrolló en múltiples ocasiones cuando las especies evolucionaban características y comportamientos útiles para trepar árboles u otras superficies verticales
